_comment_purpose: Additional seccomp denials layered atop Docker's default profile. Reference: https://docs.docker.com/engine/security/seccomp/. Applied via --security-opt seccomp=/etc/openforge/seccomp-runsc.json on every job container. gVisor's runsc itself already intercepts these syscalls in userspace; this profile is belt-and-suspenders in case runsc ever falls back to the host kernel path.
_comment_compose: defaultAction=ALLOW — this profile adds denials only. The Docker daemon's default profile (which allows ~300 syscalls) is still applied by Docker; this file narrows the set further.

syscalls.comment: Process introspection / memory RW between processes — used by debuggers and by container-escape primitives. Job containers must not be able to read each other's (or the runner's) memory.
Kernel reboot / kexec paths. A compromised container must never be able to reboot the host.
Filesystem mount manipulation. Container rootfs is mounted read-only; no remount, no chroot pivots.
Disallow changing process execution domain — used by some exploits to disable ASLR on x86.
Deny clone() with CLONE_NEWUSER (0x1000000). User namespace creation is the primary vector for unprivileged container escapes.
Deny clone3() with CLONE_NEWUSER. Same rationale as clone above; clone3 is the modern entry point on newer glibc.
Joining an existing namespace from inside a container is a known escape vector. Deny outright.
Kernel module load/unload — even with CAP_SYS_MODULE denied, this is a belt-and-suspenders block.
Storage subsystem manipulation. Job containers only read/write their tmpfs.
eBPF program load. Has been used in container-escape CVEs (CVE-2021-3490); deny outright.
